notes: Detection is purely element-level. The perElement extractor in sustainability.ts sets SUSTAIN_NO_LAZY_LOAD when el.attributes['loading'] is absent (undefined/null). The rule fires once per img element without the attribute, with selector derived from the DOM walk. Severity is always 'minor' per the evaluate() function.

cases.why: img element has no loading attribute; !loadingAttr evaluates to true in perElement, setting SUSTAIN_NO_LAZY_LOAD=true on this selector.
img element has no loading attribute; same condition as fail-1, confirms rule fires regardless of src value.
img has loading='lazy'; el.attributes['loading'] is the string 'lazy' (truthy), so !loadingAttr is false — feature not set.
img has loading='eager'; el.attributes['loading'] is the string 'eager' (truthy), so !loadingAttr is false — feature not set. The code checks attribute presence only, not the specific value.

alsoExpectNote: The perElement extractor also sets SUSTAIN_LARGE_IMAGE on fail-1 and fail-2 (src does not end in .webp or .avif), which is an element-level interaction feature. However wsg-image-format fires as a document-level finding only when networkResources contains non-next-gen image MIME types — the static fixture alone will not trigger it unless the harness supplies matching networkResources.
